title: ipsec: fix alignment check for encrypted payload data
description:
This commit fixes the alignment check for the encrypted payload data
which prevented the decryption of ESP packets for 'stream ciphers'
like AES-GCM and AES-CTR, and adds an error indicator to the dissection
tree in case the check fails. The encrypted payload data needs to satisfy
the following two conditions:

- The ciphertext length needs to be a multiple of the of the
  cipher block size.

- the ciphertext needs to terminate on a 4-byte boundary.
  (RFC 2406, section 2.4)


**Example: [ipsec-alignment-check.tgz](/uploads/3aa364f442ab627abdf3b507571f25d2/ipsec-alignment-check.tgz)**

A lot of ESP frames (11, 20, 24, 26, 28ff, ...) in the example capture file don't get decrypted and dissected by the wireshark version on the current HEAD of the master branch. With this MR branch, the packets are decrypted and dissected properly.

notes.body:
@AndersBroman, may I ask you a question, since you reviewed my last MR?

In the case of misalignment, the isakmp dissector not only adds an error text to the dissection tree item, but also an expert item:

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/fa21433c35b15cc1e2930db2ec13fb3869c4f129/epan/dissectors/packet-isakmp.c#L5950-5955

Is this helpful, should I do the same here for the ipsec dissector? The ipsec dissector currently only has one type of expert item, for the case of wrong sequence numbers.

Hi Matthias,

An expert info would be better as it would flag the packet and allow to filter it.

Ok, thanks! I hesitated a little bit to add an expert info item, because doing it is more laborious than just appending some text to the tree item. Doing both (as the isakmp dissector does) seems a bit excessive to me. What would you recommend? Just add an expert item, or add text to the tree item as well? (I noticed that the text is not wrapped, so it will be cut off when it goes beyond the window anyway.)

One argument against expert items is that it's an exceptional error which normally doesn't happen. If we would create expert items for every possible error in every payload during dissection, then dissectors would become a mess.
No, it's designed for this and not enough dissectors make use of it IMHO. I would recommend to keep the expert info instead of the text .
Ok, I'll do it.
I"m fine with a follow-up MR

@pquantin do you think this MR together with MR !3444 would qualify as bug fix for the broken AES-GCM support in the ESP dissector and acceptable for backport to release-3.4? If yes, I would be happy to prepare an MR for it.

It would be better if we could avoid backporting the full refactoring to ensure that there is no other (yet to be discovered) regression. Is there an easy way to fix the AES-GCM decryption with the ICV strip even if it is not the cleanest way of achieving it?

Hmmm... I'm not sure whether there is a quick&dirty solution. The reason why I started the refactoring in the first place is exactly because fixing AEAD support in the given implementation turned out to be too messy. What is the current timescale for the next release 3.6? If that's not too far away, it might be better to just wait for the next release.

According to https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/wikis/Development/LifeCycle 3.6 was initially planned for Q2. This will not happen obviously and we need to provide a new tentative date but it is probably not far away.
Thanks. Since I know the dissector code better now, I might take a second attempt at a simple fix for release 3.4. Otherwise, I'll just wait for release 3.6.

commits_data.title: ipsec: calculate and verified the AEAD ICV only if enabled
commits_data.message:
ipsec: calculate and verified the AEAD ICV only if enabled

AEAD ciphers should behave in the same way as the classical
cipher+hmac methods: the ICV should be calculated and verified
if the user has enabled the authentication check in the ESP
protocol options.
